title: Principles of recursive functions
concept: When a function calls itself, a new stack frame is built each time.

steps.title: Include header files
steps.explanation:
Include the standard input/output library with **`#include <stdio.h>`** for use with `printf`.

The topic of this lesson is **Recursive Function** --- a structure in which a function calls itself.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
**`int main()`** --- The starting point of the program. A main-only **stack frame** is created.

The `countdown` function defined above will not be executed because it has not yet been called.

steps.title: call countdown(3) - first recursive frame
steps.explanation: **`countdown(3);`** --- A **new stack frame** for `countdown` is stacked on top of main, with `3` copied to parameter `n`. main pauses here and waits for countdown(3) to finish.

steps.title: n=3: Output after checking termination conditions
steps.explanation: When entering countdown, we first check `if (n <= 0)`. Since `3 <= 0` is false, we skip the if block and print `"3..."` with **`printf("%d...\n", n)`**.

steps.title: call countdown(2) - second recursive frame
steps.explanation: **`countdown(n - 1);`** --- Call `countdown(2)` from within `countdown(3)`. Another new stack frame is piled on top, so there are now **3 frames** in total: main(wait) -> countdown(n=3, wait) -> countdown(n=

steps.title: call countdown(1) - third recursive frame
steps.explanation: The same process was repeated in countdown(2) with `n <= 0` false -> `"2..."` output -> **`countdown(1)`** call, raising the stack to **4th floor**. Looking at the `n` of each frame: 2nd floor `n=3`(0x1004), 3rd floor `n=2`(0x1008), 4th floor `n=1`(0

steps.title: countdown(0) - End condition reached!
steps.explanation: After outputting `"1..."` from countdown(1), call `countdown(0)`. This time `0 <= 0` is **True** --- we have finally reached the **Base Case**!

steps.title: Unwinding the stack frame
steps.explanation: As countdown(0) returns, the frame becomes **Pop**, and the waiting countdown(1) resumes. Since there is no code left, countdown(1) also returns and returns in the same order as countdown(2) -> countdown(3) -> main.

quiz.question: When countdown(3) is executed, what is the maximum number of countdown frames that exist simultaneously on the stack?
quiz.explanation:
It is called a total of 4 times: countdown(3) -> countdown(2) -> countdown(1) -> countdown(0).
When countdown(0) reaches its termination condition, there are four countdown frames on the stack simultaneously.

misconceptions.wrong: Since it is the same function when calling recursively, the same stack frame is reused.
misconceptions.correct: Each call results in a completely new stack frame.
misconceptions.why: Even if the same function is called, a separate memory space (frame) is allocated, so the n variables in each frame have independent values.

misconceptions.wrong: Recursion stops automatically without a base case.
misconceptions.correct: If there is no termination condition, it will be called infinitely, resulting in Stack Overflow.
misconceptions.why: Stack memory is finite (typically 1 to 8 MB), so if you continue to stack frames without a termination condition, you will run out of memory.

keyTakeaway: Each time a recursive function is called, a new stack frame is accumulated, and when the termination condition (base case) is reached, it is unpacked in reverse order.
